record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the Gaussian-copula approach used to generalize Grothendieck’s identity in the real case can be transferred to the complex field, and whether such a transfer would yield an analogous generalization of Haagerup’s identity for complex Gaussian random vectors.

evidence.quote: (2-RP3) Verify whether the above approach can be transferred to the complex case. Could we then similarly generalise the Haagerup identity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Haagerup's identity states that for unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\,\mathrm{sign}(\langle u,Z\rangle)\,\overline{\mathrm{sign}(\langle v,Z\rangle)}\,\bigr] \;=\; \langle u,v\rangle\cdot\, _2F_1\!\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12;2;|\langle u,v\rangle|^2\right),$$
where $Z=(Z_1,\dots,Z_n)$ is a standard complex Gaussian vector (i.e.\ $Z_j$ are i.i.d.\ with $Z_j=(X_j+iY_j)/\sqrt{2}$, $X_j,Y_j$ i.i.d.\ real standard normal), and $\mathrm{sign}(w)=w/|w|$ for $w\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$.

In the real case, one has Grothendieck's identity
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathrm{sign}(\langle u,g\rangle)\,\mathrm{sign}(\langle v,g\rangle)\bigr] \;=\; \tfrac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\langle u,v\rangle)$$
for unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $g$ standard real Gaussian, and this identity admits a generalization based on the Gaussian copula construction: for an arbitrary pair of one-dimensional distribution functions $F,G$ with quantile functions $F^{-1},G^{-1}$, the correlation between $F^{-1}(\Phi(\langle u,g\rangle))$ and $G^{-1}(\Phi(\langle v,g\rangle))$ (with $\Phi$ the standard normal CDF) is expressible as a function $\psi_{F,G}(\langle u,v\rangle)$ of the input correlation, providing a "completely correlation preserving" framework that reproduces Grothendieck's identity for the choice of $\pm 1$-valued marginals.

Problem. Determine whether the Gaussian-copula construction described above can be transferred to the complex setting—i.e., whether there exists a construction, based on the standard complex Gaussian distribution, that takes prescribed pairs of complex marginal laws (or unit-modulus marginals) and an input Hermitian correlation $\langle u,v\rangle\in\mathbb{C}$ and returns the corresponding output complex correlation as a fixed scalar function of $\langle u,v\rangle$. If such a transfer is possible, decide whether it produces an analogous generalization of Haagerup's identity, recovering Haagerup's formula in the special case where the marginals are taken to be uniform on the unit circle (i.e., the complex sign).
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023 follow-up work develops a unified real/complex Gaussian framework for "completely correlation preserving" functions and recovers Haagerup's bound for the complex Grothendieck constant, applying the formalism to multivariate Gaussian copulas. However, no source explicitly resolves whether the real Gaussian-copula generalization of Grothendieck's identity transfers verbatim to the complex case to produce a full analogous generalization of Haagerup's identity. The status is therefore not clearly established as solved.

status_evidence.title: Upper bounds for Grothendieck constants, quantum correlation matrices and CCP functions
status_evidence.snippet: Using multivariate real and complex Gaussian analysis, we provide an approach that recovers known upper bounds including Haagerup's bound for the complex Grothendieck constant, with applications to the multivariate Gaussian copula.
status_evidence.claim: A later work develops complex Gaussian / CCP-function methods related to Haagerup's identity and Gaussian copulas, but does not announce a complete complex analogue of the Gaussian-copula generalization.
